w:r.w:t: is an advanced educational tool designed to bridge the gap between passive reading and active learning. In an era of information overload, students often struggle to extract key insights from dense academic materials. This application leverages
to transform static PDF documents into interactive, conversational learning environments.
Traditional study methods often involve highlight-based reading, which is proven to be less effective for long-term retention. Students face three primary challenges:
Summarizing hundreds of pages manually is time-consuming.
It is difficult for students to test their own knowledge without external materials.
Textbooks often use jargon that requires external searching for simplification.
Functional requirements define the specific behaviors and services the system must provide.
The system shall support the upload of PDF files, extracting text while maintaining the structural integrity of chapters and sections.
The system shall use vector embeddings to retrieve the most relevant document segments to answer user queries accurately.
The AI must restrict its knowledge base to the uploaded document to ensure answers are context-specific and to mitigate the risk of AI hallucinations.
The system shall provide a "One-Click Summary" feature, generating bullet-pointed key takeaways and a glossary of technical terms found in the text.
The system shall generate at least 5 multiple-choice questions per session, providing immediate feedback and explaining the correct answer based on the document's content.
The system shall automatically detect the language (Turkish or English) and allow users to interact in their preferred language regardless of the source document's language.
For every answer provided, the system shall indicate the specific page number or section of the PDF from which the information was retrieved.
Non-functional requirements specify the criteria used to judge the operation of a system rather than specific behaviors.
The system should process a 50-page PDF document in less than 10 seconds and provide chat responses within a 3-second window.
The retrieval success rate (relevancy of the retrieved chunks) should be above 90% to ensure the AI's answers are trustworthy.
The architecture shall support documents up to 500 pages or 50MB in size without performance degradation.
The user interface (UI) shall be intuitive, requiring no technical training, and must be fully responsive for both desktop and tablet screens.
Uploaded documents should be processed in a secure environment. If local storage is used for the vector database (ChromaDB), data should not be shared with third-party training sets.
The codebase shall be modular (using LangChain), allowing for easy swapping of the AI engine without rewriting the core logic.
LangChain or LlamaIndex for RAG workflow management.
FAISS or ChromaDB for efficient document indexing.
Streamlit Framework for a responsive and clean web UI.
The primary goal is to develop a "Zero-Configuration" tool where a student can upload a syllabus or a chapter and receive a tailored study plan within seconds. By focusing on
, Lumina AI aims to increase student productivity by an estimated 40% while enhancing comprehension through interactive dialogue.

Lumina AI represents a shift from "searching for information" to "conversing with information." By combining the power of modern AI with proven learning techniques like active recall and summarization, this project provides a scalable solution for modern education challenges.
